name: Richard I's Captivity in Germany
summary: Returning from the Third Crusade, Richard I was shipwrecked near Venice and captured by Duke Leopold of Austria (whom he had insulted at Acre) in December 1192. Leopold sold him to Emperor Henry VI who demanded a ransom of 150,000 marks, roughly twice England's annual royal revenue. England was subjected to crushing taxation; silver plate was confiscated from churches. Richard was released in February 1194 after partial payment.
outcomes: Richard captured by Leopold of Austria
England taxed at unprecedented rate to pay ransom

_quarry.structural_significance: Demonstrated both the enormous financial demands of crusading and the vulnerability of even the most powerful monarch when traveling through enemy territory; the ransom taxation contributed to English baronial grievances.

sources_used: Turner & Heiser, The Reign of Richard Lionheart
